entries.title: Work style summary
entries.body: Start with the work cues, pace, and collaboration conditions that may draw your attention. Then compare environments that support this pattern with situations that make it costly. These are observation prompts, not conclusions about ability, performance, career fit, or employment decisions.
entries.module_purpose: Put the motivational differences between the primary type and Top3 into real-life task advancement methods, and make it clear that it only provides self-observation and communication clues, and cannot replace skill evidence, work experience, performance data, or organizational situation judgment.

entries.title: Collaboration advantage
entries.body: Focus on the parts where you can contribute more stably to the team, such as closing, advancing, buffering, planning, connecting or structured judgment.
entries.module_purpose: Let users see the real value they bring to collaboration, rather than a general list of advantages.

entries.title: Collaboration friction points
entries.body: Point out the friction you might create in high-pressure or noisy collaborations, and write the costs not as moral criticism but as observable inertia.
entries.module_purpose: Help users see clearly "why others are stuck with me" and provide preventive explanations for relationships and work scenarios.

entries.title: leadership model
entries.body: Write only P0 Leadership tendencies that can be published online: Are you more likely to lead through standards, results, boundaries, buffers, or support rather than writing a complete management guide.
entries.module_purpose: Provide a shareable "How do you lead people" entry to the results page, leaving structural space for subsequent workplace expansion.

entries.title: A smoother way to be managed
entries.body: Rather than writing an entire superior-subordinate pairing manual, describe what instructions, cadences, and feedback patterns may make it easier for you to stabilize.
entries.module_purpose: Turn personality reading into a more direct description of the experience of collaboration and being managed.

entries.title: relationship needs
entries.body: Use specific interaction scenarios to explain how you may express care in a relationship and how you may be misunderstood, and provide counterexamples to avoid inferring relationship needs based on type alone.
entries.module_purpose: Translate personality results into verifiable relationship communication cues: first look at the scenario, behavior and feedback, and then judge whether it fits; not a partner report, nor a conclusion about relationship needs.

entries.title: conflict script
entries.body: Break the conflict into specific triggers, current misunderstandings, and a utterable repair language to help users review the interaction instead of drawing conclusions about the relationship.
entries.module_purpose: Provide verifiable conflict scripts: identify scenarios and triggers before attempting low-stakes fixes; don’t treat type as an explanation of who is right and who is wrong.

entries.title: communication instructions
entries.body: Make communication suggestions into small cards that can be shared: first describe the situation that is easy to be misheard, and then give an expression that can be spoken.
entries.module_purpose: Provide low-certainty communication clues to help users and others calibrate facts, feelings, requests, and boundaries; do not treat types as relationship instructions or fixed rules for getting along.
